note: Runs a mortgage branch, has paid for a business coach for twelve straight years and set his own price ceiling at $10,000 before hearing the number — 'successful' and 'income' are unambiguous. He is 48, sub-10% body fat, trains jiu-jitsu two to three times a week and frames his ask as 1-2-3% tweaks rather than rescue, which is the textbook good-to-great starting point and the opposite of the 50-lb-overweight gym-averse exclusion. The one criterion he does not meet is 'neglected health' — health is not his neglected area, it is arguably his primary hobby, and he fails that test by exceeding it rather than falling short of it. Scored core on that basis, but the gap is worth recording: the stated ICP assumes a busy professional who stopped training, and this is a busy professional who never stopped and is now over-training himself into injuries. The stated ICP also has no clinical criterion, which matters here — he is mid-workup for possible gallstones with surgery on the table.
